_notes: Quotes from WebFetch of named pages 2026-10-27; fetch tool may paraphrase slightly. No ppm conversions needed. Seriously Fish gives one pH range per species; only betta gives a separate numeric preferred (wild) vs acceptable (ornamental) range. Cherrybarb/tigerbarb give qualitative preferred only.

whitecloud.ph_quote: pH: 6.0 - 8.5 (one wild reading: pH was 6.4 with low hardness values)

cpd.ph_quote: 6.5 - 7.5; a value of 7.3 was recorded at the type locality.

cherrybarb.gh_quote: 2-20 dGH. Wild fish will probably do best towards the lower end of this range.
cherrybarb.ph_quote: The farm-raised fish available in stores are fairly adaptable where water chemistry is concerned and should be happy within the range 6.0 - 8.0. Wild stock are likely to prefer slighty acidic to neutral conditions. (no number for preferred)

tigerbarb.gh_quote: Hardness: 1 - 20 dGH. Wild fish will do best towards the lower end of this range.
tigerbarb.ph_quote: pH: 5.0 - 8.0; commercial strains tend to be adaptable, but acidic to neutral conditions are recommended for wild stock. (no number for preferred)

betta.gh_quote: Hardness: 1 - 15 dGH; see comments under pH on wild vs. captive-bred fish.
betta.ph_quote: Wild-collected fish are likely to prefer a value between 5.0 - 7.0 ... ornamental strains are unfussy with a range of 6.0 - 8.0 acceptable. (box: 6.0-8.0)

dwarfgourami.ph_quote: The tank-bred fish are more adaptable and can normally be maintained anywhere within the range 6.0 - 7.5. Wild fish tend to inhabit soft, acidic water.

oscar.ph_quote: Captive-bred examples are not fussy with somewhere in the range 6.0 - 7.5 normally recommended. Wild-caught fish may require more specific conditions depending on origin.

goldfish.ph_quote: pH range: 6.0 - 8.0 (Seriously Fish has no goldfish page data)

comet.gh_quote: pH range: 6.0 - 8.0; dH range: 5 - 19 (comet is a Carassius auratus variety; same species page)

pandacory.ph_quote: pH: 6.0 to 7.4 (breeding: a pH of 6.5 should be fine)

pygmycory.gh_quote: Hardness: 2 to 15 dH but preferably below 8. (quick facts box says 0-8 dGH)

bristlenose.gh_quote: Hardness 1-15 dGH (Ancistrus cf. cirrhosus, the hobby bristlenose)

oto.gh_quote: pH range: 6.0 - 8.0; dH range: 5 - 19. (FishBase; no Seriously Fish page found at guessed slug)

sae.gh_quote: Hardness 1-15 dGH (C. langei, the fish usually sold as SAE). FishBase for C. oblongus: pH range: 6.5 - 8.0; dH range: 5 - 20 (https://www.fishbase.se/summary/Crossocheilus-oblongus.html)

hillstream.gh_quote: Hardness: 2 - 15 dGH (Beaufortia kweichowensis; hillstream is a generic name. Sewellia lineolata: pH 6.0-7.5, 1-10 dGH)

peapuffer.ph_quote: C. travancoricus prefers neutral to medium-hard water, within the range 6.8 - 8.0.

asellus.gh_quote: No hardness figure found. Only: Asellus aquaticus tends to be averse to low pH conditions but can tolerate pollution.

trumpet.gh_quote: Target 20-30C, pH 6.5-8.0, GH 6-15, KH 4-10 (Gensou care guide; unit presumed dGH, not stated)

firetoad.gh_quote: No source found giving GH or pH for Bombina orientalis (searched Wikipedia, Exo Terra, Gensou, Florida Museum etc.)

firenewt.gh_quote: No GH figure. Gensou: Singapore tap water's softness benefits newts; no remineralisation needed.
firenewt.ph_quote: Target pH 6.5-7.5, low nitrate, and absolute zero ammonia. (retailer guide, Cynops orientalis)

axolotl.gh_quote: No numeric GH. Univ. of Kentucky Ambystoma Genetic Stock Center: They need hard water to help them maintain the integrity of their skin; Never house them in extremely soft or distilled water.
axolotl.ph_quote: Keep the pH between about 6.5 and 8. (A UK vet factsheet reportedly gives 7.4-7.6; not fetched, so not recorded as preferred.)
